title: পুরুষ
Purush
Person & pronouns
blurb: Who is speaking, who is spoken to, who is spoken about, and the three levels of 'you'.

blocks.text: পুরুষ (purush) tells us who a sentence is about: the speaker, the person spoken to, or someone else. Bengali pronouns and verbs both change with the person.
Some books call the third person প্রথম পুরুষ (the first, in the Sanskrit order). Ask your teacher which labels your class uses. Bengali has no grammatical gender: সে means both 'he' and 'she'.

blocks.title: The verb changes with the person

blocks.text: Bengali has three words for 'you', and the verb ending changes with each. Choosing the right level shows respect.

head: Pronoun
Level
Used for
Example
rows: Close friends, small children, people younger than you. Rude if used wrongly.
Friends, peers, younger relatives, people you know well.
Elders, teachers, strangers, officials, polite situations.

blocks.text: When unsure, use আপনি. It is never wrong. Move to তুমি when the other person invites you to.
The third person also has an ordinary and a respectful form. The respectful form takes the same verb ending as আপনি. Words for 'this person' and 'that person' show near and far.
Pronouns change form for the object (who receives the action) and for possession. The possessive ends in -র; the object ends in -কে. In the plural, one form (-দের) does both jobs.

exercises.why: যাচ্ছ is the তুমি form of the verb.

exercises.q: Choose the form for 'saw him / her'.
exercises.why: The object form of সে is তাকে.
তোমার is the possessive of তুমি.
তিনি is the respectful third person.

exercises.why: Bengali pronouns do not show gender.

title: ক্রিয়া
Kriya
Verbs
blurb: Roots, the three forms of a verb, 'to be' and 'to have', commands, and verbs made with করা.

blocks.text: The action word of a sentence is the ক্রিয়া (kriya). Every verb is built from a root (ধাতু, dhatu). We add endings to the root to show the person and time. The dictionary form of a verb is the verbal noun, which ends in -া, like করা.
Two roots change: লেখা has the root লিখ- (likh-) in লিখি, and আসা gives এসে, এলাম. Irregular verbs are marked in the tables later.

A finite verb (সমাপিকা ক্রিয়া) ends a sentence and carries the person and time: আমি ভাত খাই। A non-finite verb (অসমাপিকা ক্রিয়া) cannot end a sentence by itself. It does not show the person or time, and it joins the main verb.

blocks.title: How they are used
items: Having eaten rice, he / she went to school. (-ে: and then)
I want to go to school. (-তে: to do)
If you go, I will go. (-লে: if)

blocks.text: In the present tense, Bengali leaves out 'is / am / are' between a noun and what it describes: আমি ছাত্র। (I am a student.) Use আছি… when you mean exist, be present or stay. To say 'have', Bengali says 'of-me there is': আমার একটা বই আছে।
A command (আদেশ) also changes with the level of 'you'. The তুই form is just the root. তুমি adds -ও / -ো. আপনি adds -ুন.
Many everyday verbs are made from a noun plus করা (do), হওয়া (become) or পাওয়া (get). The first word gives the meaning. Only the second word changes with the person and time.

exercises.q: What is the root of খাওয়া?
exercises.why: Remove the endings: the root of খাওয়া is খা.

exercises.q: In this sentence, which word is the non-finite verb?
exercises.why: খেয়ে (-ে form) joins the main verb; গেল is the finite verb.

exercises.why: 'Want to go' uses the -তে form: যেতে চাই.

exercises.q: Choose the right form ('if you go').

exercises.why: The dictionary form is the -া form: খাওয়া.

exercises.q: How do you say 'I have a book'?
exercises.why: 'Have' is expressed as 'there is' with আছে.

exercises.why: No verb is used for 'am' between a noun and a noun.

title: কাল
Kal
Tenses
blurb: Present, past and future, and how to build every tense with the right ending for each person.

blocks.text: কাল (kal) means tense. There are three times: বর্তমান (present), অতীত (past) and ভবিষ্যৎ (future). Each time has kinds: সাধারণ (simple), ঘটমান (continuing), পুরাঘটিত (completed), and for the past also নিত্যবৃত্ত (habitual).

head: Tense
English
Example
Meaning
rows: I used to eat rice every day.

blocks.text: The future continuous (খেতে থাকব) is a textbook form. In everyday speech people more often use the simple future or say 'I will be doing' with খাচ্ছি.
Take the root (করা → কর-) and add the ending for the tense and the person. The ending shows the person; the verb does not change for singular or plural (ছেলেটা যায়, ছেলেরা যায়).
Spelling varies: you may see করছো or করছ, করেছো or করেছ for তুমি. The sounds are the same.
করা (to do) is regular, so it shows the pattern clearly. Read across a row to see one tense for every person; আপনি and তিনি share the same ending.
Most verbs follow the same endings. A few change the root: খাওয়া, যাওয়া, দেওয়া and আসা change in some tenses. Learn those as they come.
যাওয়া changes its root: যা- in the present and future, গি- / গে- for completed and simple past, যে- in the habitual past.

English has tenses like 'I have been living here for two years' and 'I had been waiting for an hour'. Bengali has no separate form for these. It uses the ordinary present or past continuous and adds a time word: ধরে (for), থেকে (since), আগে (before), যখন … তখন (when … then).

head: English idea
Bengali pattern
Example
rows: has / have been doing (for a time)

rows.bn: আমি দু বছর ধরে এখানে থাকি।
rows.ro: ami du bochhor dhore ekhane thaki.

rows: has / have been doing (since a time)

rows.bn: আমি এক ঘণ্টা ধরে অপেক্ষা করছিলাম।
rows.ro: ami ek ghonta dhore opekkha korchhilam.

rows.bn: আমি যখন এলাম, তখন সে ঘুমাচ্ছিল।
rows.ro: ami jokhon elam, tokhon she ghumachchhilo.

blocks.text: 'Not yet' is এখনও … নি: আমি এখনও খাইনি (I have not eaten yet). 'Already' is ইতিমধ্যে or আগেই: সে ইতিমধ্যে চলে গিয়েছে.

Time words help you choose. রোজ (every day) and সাধারণত (usually) go with the simple present. এখন (now) goes with the continuous. ইতিমধ্যে (already) goes with the perfect. গতকাল (yesterday) goes with the simple past. আগামীকাল (tomorrow) goes with the future.
কাল (kal) means both 'yesterday' and 'tomorrow'. The verb tells you which: কাল আমি গেলাম (yesterday) and কাল আমি যাব (tomorrow). To be clear, say গতকাল (yesterday) or আগামীকাল (tomorrow).

items: Yesterday I went to the market.
When I was little I used to play in the field every day.
Tomorrow I will go to school.

exercises.why: A daily habit uses the simple present.

Choose the right form ('I have already eaten').
exercises.why: ইতিমধ্যে (already) goes with the present perfect.

-ছিলাম marks the past continuous: I was eating.

exercises.q: Choose the right verb for আপনি (tomorrow).
Choose the right verb for তুই (past).
exercises.why: তুই takes -লি in the simple past.

exercises.why: The future verb যাব shows that কাল means 'tomorrow'.

title: কারক
Karak
Case roles
blurb: The job each noun does for the verb: who acts, what is acted on, with what, for whom, from where, where.

blocks.text: কারক (karak) is the relationship between a noun and the verb. To find a noun's karak, ask the verb a question: Who does it? What is done? With what? To whom? From where? Where or when?

blocks.title: Find the karak by the question
items: Ram eats rice. রাম = কর্তা (who eats?)
Mother called the boy. ছেলেকে = কর্ম (whom?)
He / she writes with a pen. কলম দিয়ে = করণ (with what?)
Give rice to the poor person. গরিবকে = সম্প্রদান (to whom?)
Fruit falls from the tree. গাছ থেকে = অপাদান (from where?)
The bird sits on the tree. গাছে = অধিকরণ (where?)
In the morning I go to school. সকালে = অধিকরণ (when?)

blocks.text: -কে is used for both the object (কর্ম) and the one who receives (সম্প্রদান). Meaning decides: ছেলেকে ডাকলেন (called the boy) has the boy as the thing acted on. গরিবকে ভাত দাও has the poor person as the recipient of something given.
One sentence can carry several karak at once. Each noun answers a different question to the verb.

items: রাম ঘরে বসে কলম দিয়ে বন্ধুকে চিঠি লেখে।
ram ghore boshe kolom diye bondhuke chithi lekhe.
Ram, sitting at home, writes a letter to a friend with a pen.
He / she has come from Kolkata.

blocks.text: Two kinds of word are not counted as a karak because they are not directly linked to the verb.

head: Name
Job
Example
rows: Shows that something belongs to something or someone. It ends in -র / -এর.
Calls someone. It often has ও, হে, ওগো.

blocks.text: Some books count the genitive (সম্বন্ধ) as a sixth karak. Most Bengali school grammar treats it as a separate relationship.

exercises.why: বই is what is read, so it is the object.
It tells with what he / she writes.
The poor person receives the rice.
The boy is the one acted on (called).
আমার shows belonging and is not a karak.
It is used to call someone.
Time words ending in -এ are অধিকরণ (time).

title: বিভক্তি
Bibhokti
Case endings
blurb: The seven endings and little words that mark a noun, and how they change with the last sound of the noun.

blocks.text: বিভক্তি (bibhokti) is the ending or marker added to a noun to show its karak. Karak is the job; bibhakti is the mark. Traditional grammar counts seven bibhakti.
The same marker can serve two bibhakti (-কে is both 2nd and 4th). Meaning decides which one you have. Calling a person (ও রাম, হে ঈশ্বর) is the সম্বোধন, listed outside the seven.
To say 'of' or 'belonging to', add -র after a vowel sound and -এর after a consonant.

items: This is the door of the house.
This is a branch of the tree.

blocks.text: To say 'in', 'at' or 'on' a place or time, add -এ after a consonant, -তে after the vowels -ি and -ী / -ু, and -য় after -া.
Add -কে to a noun that names a person or an animal when it is the object: মাকে, বন্ধুকে, কুকুরকে. A thing you do something to usually takes no ending: আমি বই পড়ি, আমি ভাত খাই.

items: He / she wrote a letter to a friend.
I read a book. (no ending on বই)

blocks.text: Bengali often uses small words after a noun instead of an ending. They are called অনুসর্গ (onushorgo), postpositions. Words like জন্য, সঙ্গে, মধ্যে, কাছে usually follow the -র form of the noun. থেকে, দিয়ে and পর্যন্ত follow the plain noun.

exercises.why: A person who is the object takes -কে.
A thing that is read usually takes no ending.

exercises.q: -কে is the ending of which bibhakti (the object)?
exercises.why: -কে marks the object, the second bibhakti.

title: বচন
Bochon
Number & counting words
blurb: One or many: plural endings, and the little words used when counting people and things.

blocks.text: বচন (bochon) is number: একবচন (one) and বহুবচন (many). Bengali often leaves the plural out when the meaning is clear. The verb does not change for number: ছেলেটা স্কুলে যায়, ছেলেরা স্কুলে যায়।
Words like সব (all), অনেক (many) and numbers already say 'many', so the noun stays plain: অনেক ছেলে, সব বই, দুটো বই.

items: The boys are playing in the field.
The books are on the table.

blocks.text: When you count, Bengali adds a small word after the number: -টা / -টি for things, -জন for people. The noun itself does not take a plural ending.

items: There are five students in the class.

blocks.text: -টি is the more formal form of -টা: একটি বই. Do not add -গুলো after a number: say দুটো বই, not দুটো বইগুলো.
Bengali has no word for 'a' or 'the'. Instead: a plain noun is general, a number + -টা means 'one', and the noun + -টা means 'the particular one'.

exercises.q: What is the plural of ছেলে (people)?

exercises.why: Use -জন when counting people; no plural ending.
Use -টো (things) after two, and no plural ending.
The verb stays the same for one or many.
-দের is the plural for object and belonging.

exercises.q: Which counting word is for people?

title: নিষেধ ও প্রশ্ন
Nishedh o Proshno
Saying no, and asking
blurb: Negative sentences, 'is not', 'there is none', and the question words you need every day.

blocks.text: To make a sentence negative, put না after the verb for the present and the future. For the past, add -নি to the verb.
The -নি form is built on the present form of the verb for each person:
In a command, না comes after the verb too: যেও না (don't go), করো না (don't do).
To say 'am / is / are not' between two nouns, use নই, নও, নন, নয়. To say something does not exist or you do not have it, use নেই.

items: He / she is not a teacher.

blocks.text: Question words usually come just before the verb. For a yes / no question, add কি (or কী) to the sentence, or just raise your voice at the end.
Word order is subject, object, verb (SOV): আমি ভাত খাই, 'I rice eat'. The verb comes last.

exercises.why: না comes after the verb: খাই না.
The past negative adds -নি to the present form: যাইনি.
'He / she is not' is সে … নয়.

exercises.q: Choose the right word ('I have no money').
exercises.why: 'There is none / do not have' is নেই.

exercises.q: Choose the question word for 'how much'.
exercises.why: কত asks about amount or price.

exercises.q: Which sentence has the right word order?
exercises.why: The verb comes at the end: subject, object, verb.
